title: Evaluation
description:
A scored judgement of one opportunity under one named, versioned scoring model.

Evaluations are APPEND-ONLY per opportunity. Re-scoring writes a new evaluation; it never edits an old one. That is what makes two things possible: re-scoring the whole backlog under a new model and diffing the rankings to see what a weight change actually did, and detecting that an old score was computed from claims that have since been superseded. Store only a number and both are lost.

The model is recorded by id, version AND content hash, because a model file that changed underneath an evaluation makes that evaluation unexplainable.

scored_by.description: The model and the scorer fail independently, so both are recorded. This is the only place an AI provider is named anywhere in the system, and it is instance data — never core methodology.

raw.description: The measurement before normalization, in the dimension's own unit.

weight.description: Effective weight after any hypothesis multiplier, not the raw model weight.

tier.description: Forced to hypothesis when evidence_refs is empty. This is the mechanism that stops a guess being counted as a fact.

evidence_refs.description: Claim ids supporting this dimension's value.

below_min_evidence_tier.description: True when the dimension's tier is weaker than the minimum its vocabulary entry demands. A finding to raise at the gate, not a blocker.

evidence_coverage.description: Share of total weight carried by evidence-backed dimensions. Turns 'well-evidenced' into a number a gate can require.

vetoes_fired.description: Recorded by id even when empty, so a rejection is always explainable in one sentence.

ranking_note.description: Why this sits where it does relative to the rest of the shortlist. What the human actually reads at G1.
